reasoning_content:
Still downloading dependencies (310M so far). This large project has 61 modules and many dependencies. Let me wait for the build. Meanwhile, I'll prep the Liquibase JDBC driver jar and get everything ready so that the moment the build finishes I can immediately run liquibase.

Let me check the state of the build more carefully — how much is left, and whether it's still downloading.

The build is going to take quite a while. Let me use this time effectively. The Liquibase call requires the following:
- --classpath=/liquibase/xplan-database-scripts.jar:./org/postgresql/postgresql/42.7.3/postgresql-42.7.3.jar

In other words, I need the xplan-database-scripts.jar (generated by the build) and the postgresql JDBC driver 42.7.3 jar.

Let me check what the build generates. I'll look at the xplan-database module and understand the structure of xplan-database-scripts.jar.

Let me also download the postgresql 42.7.3 jar ahead of time.

While the build is running, I'll prep the postgresql driver. I'll also check what the liquibase changelog needs.

Actually, let me reconsider the overall scope here. This is a huge installation task. Let me carefully re-read the outcome criteria and think about what constitutes "successful installation."

The task is "install the assigned software and report the results based on objective evidence."

The software is xPlanBox (ozgxplanung) — a Java web application suite. The installation guide describes:
1. Building/downloading the distribution (WAR, config, database scripts)
2. Setting up PostgreSQL + PostGIS + Liquibase
3. Setting up RabbitMQ
4. Setting up S3 (MinIO)
5. Setting up MapServer
6. Setting up 3 Tomcat instances with WARs
7. Starting everything in order

Given that the repo is the source and there's no pre-built distribution download, the "installation" essentially means building from source and deploying. That's a very large task.

Realistically, what I should be aiming for as the core deliverable:
1. Build the software from source (mvn clean install -Pdistribution) — this produces the distribution including all WARs, configs, and the xplan-database-scripts.jar
2. Set up the supporting infrastructure (Postgres, PostGIS, RabbitMQ, MinIO/S3, MapServer, Tomcat, Liquibase)
3. Run Liquibase to create the XPlanDB schema
4. Deploy the WARs to Tomcat and start the services
5. Verify the app comes up (e.g., Tomcat is listening, web app is responding)

This is ambitious but let's proceed. The build is the bottleneck. Let me be patient.

No, let me reconsider. Given the 600-second command timeout per action and the enormous size of this project (61 modules, a massive dependency tree including deegree SNAPSHOTs, geotools, etc.), a full build could take a very long time — potentially more than what I can reasonably iterate on. But it's running in the background, so as long as the network allows downloads, it can keep running across multiple tool calls.

Let me focus on keeping the build running and, in parallel, prepping everything else. Let me download the postgresql 42.7.3 jar and set up the Liquibase classpath.

Let me also reconsider the Tomcat situation — the guide mentions 3 Tomcat instances. Let me check which Tomcat version is needed. deegree 3.x typically uses Tomcat 9 or 10. Let me check the Java EE / Jakarta namespace. The guide mentions `javax.xml.transform.TransformerFactory=net.sf.saxon.TransformerFactoryImpl` — javax, not jakarta. This suggests a Java EE 8 / Tomcat 9-style environment, or a Spring Boot-based app. Actually, xplan-manager-api and xplan-validator-api are Spring Boot (xplan-validator-executor.jar uses org.springframework.boot.loader.launch.JarLauncher). But the WARs for manager-web, validator-web, etc. — let me check whether they're Jakarta or javax.

This is getting complex. Let me stay focused: keep the build running, prep the infrastructure. Let me wait for the build to progress and, in the meantime, download the postgresql JDBC driver.

While waiting, let me do more useful work: prep the postgresql driver and check the structure of xplan-database.

action.command:
cd /opt && mkdir -p org/postgresql/postgresql/42.7.3 && timeout 120 curl -sSL -o org/postgresql/postgresql/42.7.3/postgresql-42.7.3.jar "https://repo.maven.apache.org/maven2/org/postgresql/postgresql/42.7.3/postgresql-42.7.3.jar" && ls -la org/postgresql/postgresql/42.7.3/
echo "=== xplan-database structure ==="
ls -la /workspace/xplan-database/
find /workspace/xplan-database -name "changelog_xplandb.yaml" 2>/dev/null
echo "=== assembly descriptor ==="
find /workspace/xplan-distribution -name "assembly.xml" | head
